options: A Boolean indicating whether a date falls within a range
A single date value
The number of days between two dates
A table of dates shifted forward or backward in time by a specified interval from the current context
questions.explain: DATEADD takes the dates currently in context and shifts every one of them by the interval you specify, returning a table meant to be used as a filter.

questions.q: In DATEADD(<dates>, <number_of_intervals>, <interval>), how is the interval argument written?
options: Unquoted, as an enumeration value like YEAR, QUARTER, MONTH, WEEK, or DAY
As a number representing days
As a quoted string like "year"
As a column reference
questions.explain: The interval is an enumeration, not a string — it should be written without quotation marks.

questions.q: Why does DATEADD handle a one-year shift better than simply subtracting 365 days?
options: It's always faster than arithmetic subtraction
DATEADD ignores leap years entirely, which is more accurate
It understands calendar units, correctly landing on the same month and day the following year regardless of leap years
Subtracting days is not supported in DAX at all
questions.explain: A fixed 365-day shift drifts across leap years. DATEADD works with actual calendar units, so a one-year shift always lands on the correct corresponding date.

questions.q: When should you reach for a specific function like PREVIOUSYEAR instead of DATEADD?
options: Specific functions only work with calculated columns, not measures
DATEADD should always be avoided in favor of specific functions
PREVIOUSYEAR is required before DATEADD can be used at all
When the shift matches one of those exact common cases and the shorter, purpose-built function reads more clearly
questions.explain: PREVIOUSYEAR, PREVIOUSMONTH, and similar functions are shortcuts for their exact case — DATEADD is more general and earns its place for shifts those shortcuts don't cover.

questions.q: In 'CALCULATE(SUM(FactInternetSales[SalesAmount]), DATEADD(DimDate[FullDateAlternateKey], -1, YEAR))', what does the -1 accomplish?
options: Reduces the measure's result by one
Filters out one row from the results
Shifts the current context's dates back one year, so the measure sums sales from the same period a year earlier
Shifts the dates forward one year
questions.explain: A negative number_of_intervals shifts dates backward in time — here, exactly one year back — giving a same-period-last-year comparison.
